papers.titleEn: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
papers.abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.
papers.filename: Yongfang Li, Science, 2026, Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules

papers.titleEn: Bioinspired and Flexible Amino Acid-Based Repairable Hybrid Architecture for Wearable Real-Time Sarin Simulant Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract The reliable room-temperature (RT) detection of organophosphorus (OP) nerve agents remains a critical challenge for public safety, hindered by sluggish diffusion and poor adsorption affinity of targets like sarin (GB) and its simulant dimethyl methylphosphonate (DMMP). Here, by mimicking the structure and function of natural enzyme, we rationally designed a bioinspired, repairable hybrid architecture that achieves highly sensitive and selective RT detection of DMMP. Our design integrates a self-assembled porous L-cystine layer derived from a two-dimensional MoS2 modified with L-cysteine. This hierarchical structure uniquely enables a synergistic “recognition-enrichment-transport-sensing” cascade elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations: the porous layer enriches DMMP molecules and facilitates their diffusion to underlying MoS2 interface, where specific adsorption triggers significant electron transfer. The sensor demonstrates an ultra-low RT practical detection limit down to 10 ppb, along with fast response, excellent selectivity, and long-term stability. Furthermore, when integrated into a flexible wearable device, the sensor exhibits outstanding mechanical bending stability and easy repairability enabled by the reversible disulfide bonds, allowing for architectural reconstruction after damage. This work offers a promising biomimetic strategy to overcome the intrinsic limitations of OP sensing and paves the way for durable, RT-wearable detection technologies in practical security applications.
papers.filename: Shuya Cao, ACS Sens., 2026, Bioinspired and Flexible Amino Acid-Based Repairable Hybrid Architecture for Wearable Real-Time Sarin Simulant Detection

papers.titleEn: Multifunctional Interface Modifier Enables High-Performance Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Wide‐bandgap (WBG, ≥1.68 eV) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) represent promising top‐cell candidates for monolithic perovskite tandem photovoltaics. However, fast crystallization kinetics of perovskite precursors and incomplete surface coverage of hole‐transporting self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) commonly degrade perovskite film quality and introduce detrimental defects at the buried interface. Herein, we report a buried‐interface engineering strategy using a rationally designed dioxaboranaphthoanthracene‐based modifier, which exhibits preferential accumulation at the perovskite buried interface. The results support additional interfacial coverage associated with DOBNA‐3PA enrichment, while modulation of perovskite crystallization kinetics enlarges grain size and reduces residual strain, contributing to improved interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the inverted 1.68 eV PSC delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.55% with an open‐circuit voltage of 1.281 V and a fill factor of 85.39%, alongside a negligible hysteresis index of 1.37%. The device retains 94% of its initial efficiency after 1800 h of storage in ambient air (40–45% relative humidity) under ISOS‐D‐1 testing protocols. Notably, this strategy exhibits outstanding generalizability across different perovskite bandgaps, enabling PCEs of 26.44% and 21.04% for 1.54 and 1.78 eV PSCs. This work establishes a dual‐function modifier strategy for improving both perovskite bulk crystallization and buried interface modification, offering a generalizable pathway toward highly efficient and stable WBG PSCs.
papers.filename: Weihua Tang, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Multifunctional Interface Modifier Enables High-Performance Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: One-Pot, Dual-Wavelength 3D Printing of Bottlebrush-Based Multimaterials
papers.abstract: Abstract Multimaterial 3D printing requires resin platforms that independently control softness, stiffness, and interfacial integrity within a single printed object. Here we demonstrate that crosslinkable bottlebrush polymers provide a versatile architecture for dual-wavelength printing of elastomers with mechanical contrast. UV irradiation (365 nm) efficiently crosslinks pendant 1,2-dithiolanes attached to the ends of polyethylene glycol side chains to form supersoft, dynamic bottlebrush networks with a tunable tensile modulus from 2 to 200 kPa by varying the lipoate content or acrylate comonomer concentration. Incorporation of an acrylate–epoxy hybrid monomer enables a second, orthogonal curing step: blue-light irradiation (460 nm) activates cationic epoxide polymerization to install a reinforcing network and increase the modulus into the MPa range, with post-cured materials reaching up to 200 MPa. This sequential radical/cationic strategy produces stiff–soft multimaterials from a single resin with high gel fractions, robust interfaces, and diffuse fracture behavior. Importantly, dual-cured networks have a higher stiffness than those obtained by curing acrylate-free resins, demonstrating that crosslinker chemistry controls network topology and mechanical properties. Together, these results establish lipoate-functional bottlebrush polymers as a modular platform for single-resin multimaterial 3D printing, where polymer architecture and temporally controlled photochemistry combine to program kPa-to-MPa mechanical contrast, degradability, and interfacial toughness.
papers.filename: Christopher M. Bates, Macromolecules, 2026, One-Pot, Dual-Wavelength 3D Printing of Bottlebrush-Based Multimaterials

papers.titleEn: Multifunctional Surface Modulation of CsPbI3 Nanocrystals Enables Stable and Efficient Quantum Dot Solar Cells
papers.abstract: All-inorganic CsPbI3 perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) represent a class of highly promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics. However, their stability is hindered by surface structural defects-primarily arising from dynamic ligand detachment-which severely compromise the stability of both the PQDs and their resulting thin films. In this study, we implement a multifunctional surface modification (MSM) strategy by introducing mono-butylammonium tetrafluoroborate (MBT) molecules to selectively passivate these surface vacancies. This approach not only stabilizes the PQD structure but also facilitates enhanced interdot electronic coupling, resulting in films with significantly reduced defect densities and improved energetic uniformity. Consequently, the MSM-treated device achieves a PCE of 15.5%, a substantial improvement over the 13.5% recorded for control devices, while exhibiting superior environmental stability. This work provides mechanistic insights into surface stabilization of CsPbI3 PQDs through a multifunctional surface modulation strategy, enabling enhanced performance and stability of PQD solar cells.
papers.filename: Jianjun Zhang, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Multifunctional Surface Modulation of CsPbI3 Nanocrystals Enables Stable and Efficient Quantum Dot Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: IMAN: An Integrated Colorimetric Sensor for Direct Detection of PD-L1 on Extracellular Vesicles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, yet early diagnosis remains difficult, highlighting the need for sensitive, noninvasive methods. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their surface proteins (e.g., PD-L1) are promising biomarkers; nevertheless, current EV detection requires time-consuming purification, sophisticated instrumentation, and long measurement protocols, resulting in high expenses and operational difficulties. This study developed an integrated colorimetric sensor, IMAN, based on a strategy of "Immunomagnetic Microbeads (IM) capture + Aptamer(Apt) recognition + Nanozyme (N) catalysis". IMAN employs magnetic beads modified with antibodies against CD9 and CD81 to directly capture EVs from serum, eliminating the need for time-consuming prior isolation; combined with a one-step colorimetric readout, the entire workflow can be completed with only ∼40 min of hands-on time, requiring no complex instrumentation. The PD-L1 protein on the EV surface is specifically recognized by a nanoparticle-bound nucleic acid aptamer. Signal generation is achieved through the catalytic oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) by a platinum-gold bimetallic nanozyme (Pt@Au). The facile IMAN colorimetric method demonstrated a relatively broad dynamic range (107-1010 particles/mL), high specificity (unaffected by 100 pg/mL soluble PD-L1 in serum), and reproducibility (relative standard deviation, RSD = 9.1%). Analysis of clinical serum samples revealed significantly elevated EV-PD-L1 levels in patients with lung cancer compared with healthy donors and patients with benign nodule (p < 0.01). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis yielded areas under the curve (AUC) of 0.849 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from healthy donors and 0.860 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from patients with benign nodules, which are superior to those of the conventional serum biomarkers CEA and Cyfra21-1. By addressing the cost, complexity, and slow response of current methods, IMAN offers a simple, cost-effective platform for direct EV surface protein detection without complex instrumentation, providing a novel tool for the noninvasive lung cancer diagnosis.
papers.filename: Yanlian Yang, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, IMAN An Integrated Colorimetric Sensor for Direct Detection of PD-L1 on Extracellular Vesicles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
